vibe: A quiet-ish Sunday with two exploited Windows/Cisco zero-days still in the wild, Anthropic eyeing a record IPO, and the cloud giants swapping olive branches on multicloud.

cyber.title: Lazarus exploits Windows afd.sys zero-day (CVE-2026-68820) for SYSTEM access
cyber.summary: North Korea's Lazarus group is chaining an actively-exploited use-after-free in the WinSock driver (afd.sys) to elevate to SYSTEM and drop a backdoor at defence/aerospace firms. It's patched in August Patch Tuesday — if any Windows box slipped that cycle, prioritise it.

cyber.title: Cisco FMC zero-day (CVE-2026-20316) under active exploitation, added to CISA KEV
cyber.summary: Static credentials let unauthenticated attackers reach sensitive data on Cisco's Firewall Management Center. Now in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog — patch or restrict management-plane access.

cyber.title: Hackers infect Android car head units with proxy botnet malware
cyber.summary: Aftermarket Android head units are being enrolled into a residential proxy botnet via malicious firmware/apps — turning cars into traffic-laundering nodes. A reminder that the IoT attack surface now includes the dashboard.

ai.title: Anthropic prepping what could be one of the largest IPOs ever
ai.summary: Reports say Anthropic's planned public debut could match or exceed SpaceX's record — with 300k+ business customers now on the books. A signal of how fast the frontier-lab economy is maturing into public markets.

ai.title: Anthropic brings Claude Mythos 5 into Claude Security for enterprise teams
ai.summary: Anthropic is wiring its newest Mythos 5 model into Claude Security, aimed at enterprise SOC/appsec workflows. Worth a glance if your team is evaluating LLM-assisted security tooling.

ai.title: Anthropic appears to be A/B testing reduced effort levels in Claude Code
ai.summary: Devs on HN noticed Claude Code quietly serving lower-effort responses to some users — an A/B test on reasoning budget. Directly relevant if you're leaning on it day-to-day; explains occasional 'feels dumber today' moments.

ai.title: Cloudflare launches Kitesurf, a browser runtime built for AI agents
ai.summary: Runs on Cloudflare Workers, uses ~3-7x less CPU/memory than Chromium and passes 235k+ web-platform tests. A cloud-native answer to the headless-browser cost problem for agentic workloads — squarely in your lane.

ai.title: Salesforce partners say Agentforce isn't yet moving meaningful revenue
ai.summary: A useful reality check: channel partners aren't seeing the agentic-AI pipeline Salesforce hyped. The gap between AI-agent marketing and booked revenue remains wide.

ai.title: OpenAI urges California to strengthen its AI safety bill
ai.summary: OpenAI publicly backed tougher California AI-safety legislation (corroborated by TechCrunch). Notable given the industry's usual allergy to regulation — read as positioning ahead of federal rules.

it.title: AWS and Google Cloud link up to ease multicloud deployments
it.summary: The two rivals launched a joint offering to simplify connecting workloads across both platforms, with Azure expected to join the multicloud networking product later. Direct relevance for anyone architecting cross-cloud infra.

it.title: Cloud-native roundup: GKE dynamic storage class, Azure AKS AI infra
it.summary: GKE now auto-picks Persistent Disk vs Hyperdisk per node hardware; Azure AKS is pushing bare-metal + fleet management for AI training/inference. Incremental but handy quality-of-life wins if you run managed Kubernetes.

videos.title: China moves to Linux, WSL beats native installs, potato gaming PCs fixed - Linux Weekly News
videos.verdict: SKIM — solid open-source roundup, but nothing you must act on
videos.summary: China ordered govt agencies to drop Windows 10 (China Gov Edition) for a homegrown distro (likely Kylin OS or UnionTech) years ahead of schedule — digital-sovereignty play. Kernel 7.3 gets a Valve-contributed VRAM-management fix so low-VRAM (8GB) GPUs degrade gracefully instead of crashing. Also: WSL usage reportedly outgrowing native Ubuntu installs, plus more Google/Apple 'malicious compliance' with court orders.
